meta.title: A Whale in the Hall
meta.textType: functional: a guide's talk with numbers, a blog post

paragraphs: Posted by Lily. On Saturday, December twelfth, the Explorers visited the science museum. Teacher Kim, Mia, Leo, and May came with me. At half past ten, an assistant met us at the entrance. We had a group pass, and we walked into the main hall. The hall is very high, and a huge blue whale hangs near the ceiling. It is only a model, but it looks real. Teacher Kim will read my post first, and then she will put it on the blog.

At eleven o'clock, Guide Ann stood under the whale and gave a talk. She wore a name badge on a cord, and she smiled at all of us. "This model is exactly twenty-five meters long," she said. "A real blue whale can weigh one hundred fifty thousand kilograms." "That is as much as thirty elephants." "The blue whale is the biggest animal on our planet." "It is well known all over the world."

Guide Ann pointed at the whale's chest. "Its heart weighs about as much as a motorbike," she said. "A baby whale is seven meters long when it is born." "A blue whale does not have one single tooth." "It eats about four tons of tiny sea animals every day." "That is almost forty million of them!" We wrote the numbers in our notebooks. "How heavy is a baby whale?" asked Leo. "About two tons," said Guide Ann.

Guide Ann also told us about the scientists. "An international team of scientists measured a whale like this one," she said. "They came from many countries." "Scientists study whales because they want to keep them safe." Mia asked, "How long does a blue whale live?" "About eighty years," said Guide Ann.

After the talk, we went to a touch screen near the whale. The screen said "WHALE QUIZ", "Touch START", and "Choose A, B, or C". Leo touched START. The first question was, "How long is the model?" Leo chose A, "twenty-five meters". The screen turned green and said, "Great answer!" Mia read the words out loud. Then Teacher Kim held the end of a long strip of yellow tape on the floor. Leo stood at the start, and the end had a mark for twenty-five meters. May and I walked next to the tape and counted our steps. What is your favorite animal? Which numbers do you know about it?
